text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000216 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, but the small set of returned charts mostly supports the billed level, so the documentation itself needs scrutiny before a conclusion.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claim pattern is not what a sicker panel would explain: 99215 use is elevated in every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are for routine problems such as UTI, upper respiratory infection, rash, back pain and follow-up visits (e.g., C0109339, C0109405, C0109343, C0109767). Against that, the documented 99215s only modestly exceed the comparison unsupported rate, and with 2 of 20 claims this is too small a difference to call meaningful. Records cover only a small share of claims, and the charts that support high MDM may themselves be inflated. C0109343, a rash visit in a 23-year-old with no chronic conditions, is documented as high MDM. Many supported 99215 notes record no minutes. A third of notes carry a problems flag, some show repeated times, and no audit trail was received. A reviewer should first pull the full notes for the low-complexity 99215s with high documented MDM (starting with C0109343 and the problems-flagged examples C0109340 and C0109473). They should check whether the MDM elements reflect a real encounter or templated text, and should request the EHR audit trail and a larger records sample to test whether the documentation holds up."}
